reason: E1 shows that severe lattice distortion in BCC HEAs makes edge dislocation motion more difficult, not easier, contradicting the premise that distortion reduces the Peierls barrier and activates more slip. E2 demonstrates DRX and GBS in a different BCC HEA at 1000–1200 °C, providing partial support for dynamic recovery at high temperature, but the cited evidence does not link these mechanisms to lattice distortion or to the specific WTaTiVZr alloy. The key causal chain from lattice distortion to enhanced plasticity is unsupported or contradicted by the cited passages.
premises: Severe lattice distortion in BCC HEAs alters dislocation behavior, producing wavy edge dislocations and making edge motion more difficult
In a BCC refractory HEA (TaNbHfZrTi), dynamic recrystallization and grain boundary sliding occur at 1000–1200 °C, causing flow stress drop and steady-state flow
Lattice distortion in the WTaTiVZr alloy will reduce the effective Peierls barrier and activate additional slip systems
Dynamic recovery mechanisms (grain boundary sliding, dynamic recrystallization) will enhance plastic strain and crack-tip blunting in the WTaTiVZr alloy
